Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model for Interest Rate Modeling

Source: R/dnsr-package.R
dnsr-package.Rd

A comprehensive toolkit for modeling, fitting, and simulating interest rates using the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel (DNS) model. The package provides functions to calibrate the DNS model from yield curve data, estimate factor dynamics, simulate yield curves, and visualize results.

Details

The Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model is a popular term structure model used in finance for modeling the yield curve. It represents the yield curve using three latent factors (level, slope, and curvature) that evolve over time according to a mean-reverting stochastic process.

This package provides a comprehensive implementation of the DNS model, including:

  • Data retrieval and processing of U.S. Treasury yield curve data

  • Cross-sectional fitting of the Nelson-Siegel model to yield curves

  • Time-series estimation of factor dynamics

  • Stochastic simulation of interest rate paths

  • Visualization tools for yield curves and factor analysis

The package is designed to be used by financial analysts, risk managers, and researchers for applications such as:

  • Interest rate forecasting and scenario analysis

  • Risk management and stress testing

  • Pricing and valuation of fixed income securities

  • Asset-liability management

Key Functions

Download and process Treasury yield curve data

get_treasury_yield_combined

Get historical and current Treasury yield data

fit_ns_model

Fit Nelson-Siegel model to a single yield curve

fit_dns_model

Fit Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model to time series of yield curves

estimate_dns_dynamics

Estimate dynamics of the DNS factors

get_calibrated_dns_params

Get calibrated DNS parameters from market data

simulate_dns_factors

Plot yield curves and fitted DNS models

plot_factor_time_series

Plot DNS factor time series

Model Background

The Nelson-Siegel model expresses the yield curve as: $$y(m) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m}\right) + \beta_3 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m} - e^{-\lambda m}\right)$$ where \(m\) is maturity, \(\beta_1\), \(\beta_2\), and \(\beta_3\) represent the level, slope, and curvature factors, respectively, and \(\lambda\) controls the decay rate of factor loadings.

In the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model, these factors follow a mean-reverting stochastic process: $$d\beta(t) = \kappa(\theta - \beta(t))dt + \sigma dW(t)$$ where \(\kappa\) is the speed of mean reversion, \(\theta\) is the long-run mean, \(\sigma\) is the volatility, and \(W(t)\) is a Wiener process.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Get Treasury yield data
yield_data <- get_treasury_yield_combined("2020-01-01")

# Fit DNS model
dns_result <- fit_dns_model(yield_data, n_days = 100)

# Estimate factor dynamics
dynamics <- estimate_dns_dynamics(dns_result$parameters)

# Simulate future yield curves, starting from the most recent fitted factors
latest <- dns_result$parameters[which.max(dns_result$parameters$Date), ]
params <- dns_dynamics_to_sim_params(dynamics, lambda = latest$lambda)
sim_result <- simulate_dns_yield_curves(
  params = params,
  initial_factors = as.numeric(latest[c("beta1", "beta2", "beta3")]),
  maturities = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30),
  n_paths = 100,
  engine = "exact"
)

# Visualize results
plot_yield_curves(yield_data, dns_result)
plot_factor_time_series(dns_result)
plot_simulated_yields(sim_result)
} # }
